answer: Cheap grader aliases used to cash several seats from one operator until identity itself became expensive to split. Each rater now cuts a personal onyx plaque, pins it to a numbered mesa post that only that key can move, and sends four nectar drips 14 minutes apart through distinct relay stations. The plaque bond locks 10.2 stake-units for 52 hours. Auditors reweigh every drip against public relay receipts and slash a plaque or post reused under two names. If two identities share one mesa post, or a nectar interval skips a relay, the plaque bond is burned.
